CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What is vectra

An R package implementing a columnar query engine for larger-than-RAM data. It provides dplyr-like verbs (filter, select, mutate, group_by, summarise, joins, window functions) backed by a pure C11 pull-based execution engine and a custom on-disk format (.vtr). All operations are lazy until collect() materializes results.

# Full check (compiles C, runs tests, checks NAMESPACE)
"/mnt/c/Program Files/R/R-4.6.0/bin/Rscript.exe" -e 'devtools::check(args = "--no-manual")'

# Run all tests
"/mnt/c/Program Files/R/R-4.6.0/bin/Rscript.exe" -e 'devtools::test()'

# Run a single test file

# Load for interactive testing
"/mnt/c/Program Files/R/R-4.6.0/bin/Rscript.exe" -e 'devtools::load_all(); tbl(f) |> collect()'

Architecture

Execution model: lazy pull-based pipeline

All user-facing verbs (filter, select, mutate, etc.) build a tree of vectra_node objects in R. Each node wraps a C-level VecNode external pointer. No data moves until collect() calls C_collect, which pulls VecBatch structs through the node tree one row group at a time.

On-disk format (.vtr, tdc container)

Binary columnar format produced by src/vtr1_tdc.c. A file is a tdc heterogeneous container (TDC1 magic + attached schema + trailing row-group index) holding one self-describing tdc_block_record per column per row group, followed by a 24-byte vectra trailer (container_len u64, digest u64, version u32, "VTRD", see src/vtr1_tdc.h). The digest is a VtrDigest (src/vtr_digest.h) over every byte the writer hands tdc, computed through a digesting sink on the tdc io callbacks; the extender/widener seed it with the pre-append store fingerprint, rewrite the trailer past the new end, and restore the old trailer on abort. The trailer is honoured only when it ends the file exactly where the header says the container ends, and older readers ignore it (the tdc decoder never looks at file length). vtr1_tdc_fingerprint() = digest of (trailer digest or its absence, column types, whole row-group index incl. block offsets/sizes/stats); for trailer-less stores it is layout-only, which does NOT separate same-shape stores (measured: the #13 repro pair collides without the trailer). Columns are stored as typed arrays with validity bitmaps for NA support.

  • write_vtr() writes from R data.frames via Vtr1TdcWriter (vtr1_open_tdc_writer → append_rowgroup → close).
  • tbl() opens for lazy reading via Vtr1TdcFile (vtr1_open_tdc); the scan node fseek/freads raw block bytes recorded in the row-group index and hands them to vtr_decode_column_tdc.
  • The legacy v4 codec (custom encoding tags, shuffle+LZ/deflate packaged in-tree) was ripped out in April 2026; tdc is the sole codec path. The .vtr format is no longer backwards-compatible with pre-rewire files.

Encode pipeline (src/vtr_codec_tdc.c, driven by comp_level + optional quantize/spatial specs): 1. vtr_codec_tdc_prepare_request builds a tdc_block view over a VecArray and derives a tdc_codec_spec (model / transform chain / entropy). 2. tdc_encode_block emits a single self-describing tdc_block_record (header + side-meta + payload + validity). 3. tdc_stream_encoder_write_block records the record into the container’s row-group index and attaches per-column min/max/null_count stats (Vtr1ColStat) for scan-side predicate pruning.

comp_level values: VTR_COMPRESS_NONE (passthrough), VTR_COMPRESS_FAST (default heuristic: BSHUF + LZ, run at VTR_FAST_LZ_LEVEL = tdc level 1, the flat-hash matcher; tdc’s default chained level was ~15x slower on double columns for 1-3 pp of ratio, gcol33/tdc#1, and was the whole write_vtr() sink gap in #26), VTR_COMPRESS_SMALL (try-all-pick-smallest). SMALL calls vtr_codec_tdc_optimize_small (src/vtr_codec_tdc.c): after prepare_request builds the FAST baseline spec, it enumerates per-column candidate specs — varying the model (RAW / DELTA / DELTA2 / FPC / DICT_NUMERIC / SPARSE_ZERO for numerics, DICT_1D for strings; the fused model is fixed when quantize/spatial is active) crossed with the entropy coder (LZ / LZ_OPT / LZ_SPLIT / FSE / HUFFMAN4, plus per-lane LANE where a byte-shuffle exposes fixed-width lanes) — trial-encodes each candidate and keeps the smallest record. The candidate sweep runs in parallel (each thread encodes a disjoint slice into its own scratch buffer, smallest reduced under a critical section); it stays serial for small blocks and when already inside a parallel region. Ties break to the lowest candidate index, so the chosen spec — and the bytes on disk — are independent of thread count. The FAST spec (including its level-1 LZ) is always a candidate, so SMALL is never larger than FAST (measured ~16-40% smaller on mixed data). The reader is generic (decodes off the self-describing record header), so no decode-side change is needed. Encode-time cost is higher (N trial encodes per column); that is the intended SMALL tradeoff.

C engine (src/)

Pure C11. Compression goes through vendored tdc (src/tdc/); TIFF deflate and gzipped CSV input go through vendored miniz (src/miniz/). No external zlib link. Key types in src/types.h: - VecType: int64, double, bool, string - VecArray: single column with validity bitmap and type-punned data union - VecBatch: row group (n columns + optional selection vector for zero-copy filtering) - VecNode: pull-based plan node with next_batch() and free_node() vtable

Plan nodes (each in its own .h/.c pair): - scan (vtr file reader with zone-map pruning, binary search, and hash index pushdown) -> filter -> project (select/mutate/rename) -> sort -> limit - topn (combined sort+limit optimization) - group_agg (hash-based grouping + aggregation: n, sum, mean, min, max, n_distinct, median) - join (hash join: left, inner, right, full, semi, anti) - fuzzy_join (levenshtein/DL/Jaro-Winkler distance joins) - window (row_number, rank, dense_rank, lag, lead, cumsum, cummean, cummin, cummax) - concat (union / bind_rows) - block (block-nested-loop join helper)

Expression evaluation (src/expr.h, src/expr.c, src/expr_string.c, src/expr_geom.c, src/expr_seq.c): - Variable-arity children array on VecExpr supports N-arg functions - String ops: paste/paste0 (N-ary), grepl/gsub/sub (fixed + POSIX regex with backreferences), str_extract (regex capture groups), toupper/tolower/trimws/nchar/substr/startsWith/endsWith - Fuzzy matching: levenshtein, dl_dist, jaro_winkler (OpenMP parallelized) - Control flow: case_when, coalesce, ifelse - Set ops: %in% with hash set acceleration for large sets - Geometry ops (EXPR_GEOM, src/expr_geom.c): the st_* functions usable inside mutate/filter/summarise (st_area, st_length, st_distance, st_centroid, st_buffer, st_intersects, …), dispatched on a single geom_fn char. They decode the hex-WKB geometry string column with GEOS one row at a time (per-thread GEOS_init_r contexts, OpenMP schedule(dynamic, 256) so validity bytes stay disjoint), no per-batch sf round-trip. A binary op’s second geometry (right) is a geometry column or, when a constant sf/sfc, a hex-WKB string literal parsed once and shared read-only across threads — the same cross-context sharing the streaming spatial verbs use. Serializer: .serialize_geom in R/expr.R; doc topic ?geom_expressions in R/geom_expr.R. - Sequence ops (EXPR_SEQ, src/expr_seq.c): the seq_* functions over an ASCII sequence string column (seq_length, seq_gc, seq_revcomp, seq_complement, seq_reverse, seq_transcribe, seq_translate standard genetic code, seq_subseq, seq_dist reusing the strdist_* kernels), dispatched on a single seq_fn char. Per-row decode, two-pass string build (serial offset assignment then parallel fill into disjoint slices); complement carries the IUPAC ambiguity codes, NA/unparseable cells yield NA. Serializer: .serialize_seq in R/expr.R; doc topic ?seq_expressions in R/seq_expr.R.

Aggregation (src/agg_ops.h, src/agg_ops.c): - n_distinct: per-group open-addressing hash set (FNV-1a, 70% load factor) - median: per-group dynamic array + qsort

Hash indexes (src/vtri.h, src/vtri.c): - .vtri sidecar files naming the row groups that may hold a key, for equality predicates - one format (v5) covering single-column and composite indexes: header (column indices, case-insensitive flag, build stamp) then 12-byte (hash u64, rowgroup u32) entries sorted ascending, then a directory giving the first entry per leading-hash-bit prefix - one entry per (distinct key, row group), not per row, so an index over a low-cardinality column stays the same size as the store grows - Case-insensitive index option; composite keys combine per-column FNV-1a hashes - Accelerates == and %in%; composites accelerate AND-combined equality predicates - scan.c detects index-eligible predicates and prunes row groups via bitmap

OpenMP parallelization (src/vec_omp.h): - CPU-bound string ops (grepl regex, levenshtein, dl_dist, jaro_winkler) use #pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 64) with threshold n > 1000 - Per-thread regex compilation for thread safety - OpenMP flags already in Makevars/Makevars.win - Never #include <omp.h> in any src/*.c; include "vec_omp.h" instead. It forward-declares the handful of runtime functions we use (omp_get_max_threads, omp_get_thread_num, omp_in_parallel, omp_set_num_threads) and never pulls in the clang omp.h wrapper. #pragma omp directives need no header. Two CRAN clang flavors shipped an omp.h that breaks when included after R’s headers — clang 21’s unbalanced declare variant pragma (archived 0.5.1) and clang 22’s declare variant match(...) clause that R’s match->Rf_match macro mangles (broke 0.9.1 on r-devel-linux-x86_64-fedora-clang). Direct <omp.h> includes have twice cost a CRAN archival/breakage; the rule exists to prevent a third.

Format backends (scan + write, each in own .h/.c pair): - csv_scan / csv_write: streaming CSV with type inference from first 1000 rows - sql_scan / sql_write: SQLite read/write via embedded sqlite3 (sqlite_format.c) - tiff_scan / tiff_write: GeoTIFF raster read/write (pixels → rows with x, y, band columns). parquet_scan (src/parquet_scan.c on parquet_column.c, parquet_meta.c, parquet_thrift.c, parquet_codec.c): native reader behind tbl_parquet(), scan-only, no arrow. Thrift compact footer and page headers decoded with every read bounds-checked; one node covers a list of files (first file’s schema, later files matched by name, vectra types must agree). Per row group each needed column chunk is read whole (compressed) and decoded page by page by a PqCursor; fixed-width pages and dictionaries are converted to the output type once so emitting is a memcpy; columns decode in parallel, cursors never raise and the node raises after the region. SNAPPY/LZ4 in-tree, GZIP via miniz, ZSTD via the vendored decoder in src/zstd/; BROTLI/LZO error naming the column. The scan owns an AND-combinable pruning predicate (parquet_scan_predicate_slot) that the optimizer fills like a .vtr scan’s, checked through the shared predicate_might_match against footer statistics (unsigned and byte-array bounds only from min_value/max_value). Scan-only text backends (no write pair) share byte_reader (plain + gzip via miniz): - fasta_scan: FASTA/FASTQ records → rows (id, desc, seq, +qual) - bed_scan: BED features → rows (fixed BED schema by column count; start 0-based, end half-open, read faithfully; feeds interval_join for genome-interval overlap)

Write control (src/vtr_write.h, src/vtr_write.c): - vtr_write_node_batched(): accumulates rows from upstream batches using VecArrayBuilder, flushes when buffer reaches target batch_size - Exposed via write_vtr(node, path, batch_size = NULL). Default for data.frames: 131072 rows (cache-friendly for decompression). For nodes: NULL (one row group per upstream batch).

Growing a store in place, two directions, one mechanism: - Rows (src/vtr_append.c + the extender in src/vtr1_tdc.c, append_vtr(along = "rows")): existing row groups are never read. tdc’s tdc_stream_encoder_open_extend appends the new blocks and a rebuilt index past the old trailer, then patches the 64-byte header last, so the cost tracks the appended rows and an interrupted append leaves the pre-append container intact (vtr1_abort_tdc_extender truncates the orphaned bytes). The index entries describing the existing row groups are carried over verbatim – they stay correct because nothing before the old trailer moves. This is what makes building a store by repeated appends linear rather than quadratic; before 0.11.9 the row path restreamed the whole file through a fresh writer into a temp file and swapped it, so each call cost a full pass over the store (issue #10, measured slope 0.0215 s/MB, now 0.00006 s/MB with per-call time flat from 4 MB to 112 MB). The row path honours compress; it used to hardcode VTR_COMPRESS_FAST. - Columns (src/vtr_append_cols.c + the widener in src/vtr1_tdc.c, append_vtr(along = "cols")): existing columns are never read. tdc’s tdc_stream_encoder_open_widen appends the new blocks, a replacement schema, and a rebuilt index past the old trailer, then patches the 64-byte header last, so the cost tracks the appended columns and an interrupted append leaves the pre-widen container intact (vtr1_abort_tdc_widener also truncates the orphaned bytes so repeated failures cannot grow the file). Row-group boundaries and existing block offsets are unchanged, so .vtri indexes over the original columns survive. The driver’s only real job is chunking: row-group boundaries are fixed by the existing file, so incoming batches are cut at those boundaries via vec_builder_append_range (each row copied exactly once between arriving and being encoded). A row-count mismatch can only be detected at the end, so it aborts rather than committing a partial widen.

R-to-C bridge split across multiple files registered in src/init.c: - src/r_bridge.c: core entry points (tbl, collect, explain) - src/r_bridge_core.c: expression parsing (R list → VecExpr) - src/r_bridge_nodes.c: verb node creation (filter, project, sort, group_agg, window, join, etc.) - src/r_bridge_io.c: format read/write entry points - src/r_bridge_index.c: index creation/querying entry points

R layer (R/)

  • tbl.R: Entry points for all format backends: tbl() (vtr), tbl_csv(), tbl_sqlite(), tbl_xlsx(), tbl_tiff().
  • write.R: Writers for all formats: write_vtr(), write_csv(), write_sqlite(), write_tiff(). Writers are S3 generics dispatching on vectra_node (streaming) and data.frame. Node-level batch_size parameter controls output row group size.
  • expr.R: NSE expression serializer. Captures R expressions (arithmetic, comparison, boolean, case_when, coalesce, multi-arg paste/paste0, regex grepl/gsub/sub, str_extract, %in%) into nested lists that the C bridge interprets. This is the translation layer between dplyr-style expressions and the C engine.
  • verbs.R: All dplyr verb implementations as S3 methods on vectra_node. Verbs build new nodes via .Call() to C entry points.
  • verbs_grouping.R: group_by(), summarise(), count()/tally(). Native C aggregations: n(), sum(), mean(), min(), max(), n_distinct(), median().
  • joins.R: Join verbs + parse_join_keys() for by argument handling. Includes fuzzy joins.
  • across.R: across() expansion for mutate/summarise.
  • windows.R: Window function detection and node creation.
  • bind.R: bind_rows() (streaming ConcatNode when schemas match, R fallback otherwise) and bind_cols().
  • reframe.R: Variable-length summarise via collect() fallback.
  • index.R: create_index() (single or composite multi-column) and has_index() for .vtri sidecar hash indexes.
  • block.R: Block lookup utilities.
  • explain.R: Prints the query plan tree for debugging.

Column type mapping

R integers are stored as VEC_INT64 internally and returned as double by default (no native int64 in base R). bit64::integer64 support is optional via Suggests.

Key Design Decisions

  • No Rcpp: Direct .Call() interface to C via registered routines. No C++ in vectra’s own source (GEOS C++ lives in the libgeos dependency, reached through its C API — see below).
  • Prefer libgeos over sf: Geometry operations are built on the GEOS C API supplied by libgeos (LinkingTo: libgeos, symbols resolved at load via R_GetCCallable), not by delegating to sf. libgeos is ~2.8 MB (GEOS only) against sf’s ~138 MB (GEOS + GDAL + PROJ), needs no system dependency, and lets the compute path run in C straight off the .vtr hex-WKB geometry column with no R round-trips. New spatial work goes pure-libgeos; sf stays a Suggests only for the pieces libgeos cannot cover (vector format I/O = GDAL, reprojection/warp = PROJ). Do not reach for sf when a GEOS C call exists.
  • Self-overlay = per-component polygonize, tiled + streamed (src/vtr_overlay.c, R/spatial.R): C_overlay_partition parses each feature once, in parallel – repair (GEOSMakeValid), areal-only, snap (GEOSGeom_setPrecision) – returning cleaned WKB + bounding boxes + connected components. The R driver makes each component one overlay job; C_overlay_run nodes a job’s boundary linework once (GEOSUnaryUnion), polygonises it (GEOSPolygonize), and labels each face by point-in-poly (GEOSPointOnSurface + GEOSPreparedIntersects over a GEOSSTRtree). One noding pass per job, so cost tracks the number of faces, not overlap multiplicity. The alternative – iterated binary GEOSIntersection/GEOSDifference (QGIS-style union) – is grid-free but ~O(cells x multiplicity); on a 1781-feature WDPA slice (~20x multiplicity) binary was 71 s and 1.7% off, polygonize 12 s and exact.
  • Bounded memory by component-then-tile, clean once (the reason this exists – the friend chose vectra so RAM would not explode): a single connected component of many large overlapping polygons noded monolithically blows up (~340 MB WKB -> 45 GB). So components too large for the budget are tiled over their own extent and clipped (GEOSClipByRect), and features are cleaned exactly once (in partition) rather than re-repaired per tile. Jobs run one per OpenMP thread (threads, default min(cores, 8)) and stream to .vtr in batches sized to mem_limit (default 2 GB; vectra.overlay_mem_limit/vectra.overlay_threads). The full 470k-feature WDPA/bathymetry layer overlays in ~24 min at ~16 GB peak (8 threads); the same layer was 42 GB and OOM-bound monolithic, and plain sf::st_intersection() cannot do it at all. Tuning: raise mem_limit/threads for speed, lower for tighter memory; tiling splits some pieces along internal tile edges (coverage and labels stay exact, so downstream per-piece resolution is unaffected).
  • Snapping grid is checked, not assumed: polygonize needs inputs snapped so the near-duplicate boundaries overlapping polygons share coincide; otherwise the arrangement carries sliver faces. The grid (.overlay_grid) is magnitude-relative (max|bbox| * 3e-8, ~7.5 significant digits, unit-invariant); the exact-coverage band is wide (~0.2-1.0 m on the WDPA data). The C engine returns each piece’s and input’s area and spatial_overlay() checks the coverage invariant per batch (piece areas covering an input sum to its area), warning if it drifts past 1e-4 rather than returning silently wrong. (The C GEOSGeom_setPrecision path also handles coarse grids that the older R st_set_precision + st_make_valid snap threw on.)
  • Optimizer rewrites are order-independent (src/optimize.c): column pruning propagates through a ProjectNode by first dropping pass-through entries the parent does not need (at least one column is kept so batches carry a row count), so a scan below mutate() reads only used columns. Predicate pushdown leaves the FilterNode in place and attaches a pruning-only copy of its predicate to every .vtr scan reachable through project (renames followed), other filters, sort, and each type-compatible ConcatNode child; conjuncts on computed or overwritten columns are dropped from an AND (safe: the filter above still evaluates every row), and an OR/negation that cannot travel whole is not pushed. The copy never crosses limit, top-n, window, aggregate or join. The filter records that it pushed, so explain() then collect() does not stack copies. Joins get neither rewrite yet (output-column provenance is not tracked). Cross-checked against base R in test-optimize-rewrites.R.
  • spatial_join is a lazy node (src/spatial_join.c): the native path builds a SpatialJoinNode. The resident y is held as a GEOS locator (geometries + STRtree) plus its attribute columns as one C batch; left batches stream and are matched in one OpenMP pass via vtr_geos_match_batch (which calls the existing named per-thread workers, keeping the clang function-sanitizer pattern), then gathered in C, so the result feeds the next verb with no spill and no R data-frame buffering. R decides the output layout (names, suffixes, out_geom, geometry last) and passes one source per output column. coords= points are written directly as hex WKB, byte-identical to the GEOS writer. keep_geom = FALSE drops the left geometry on every path and skips encoding points at all.
  • Selection vectors: VecBatch.sel enables zero-copy filtering (filter node sets a selection vector rather than copying rows).
  • nrow() answers from metadata or says it does not know (src/node_rows.c, VecNode.static_rows, R/dim.R): dim.vectra_node (which is what makes base nrow()/ncol() work, both being dim(x)[i]) reads an optional per-node vtable hook giving the exact rows a node will emit without pulling a batch, so it neither runs nor consumes the plan — unlike every terminal op, which takes the node. A scan reads its row-group index (minus tombstone->n deletions, when every tombstoned index is in range); project/dropcol/rowid/sort/window delegate to their child; limit/topn clamp it; concat sums. Nodes whose output length depends on the data (filter, joins, group_agg, distinct) and the format scans that carry no stored count (CSV/SQLite/TIFF) leave the hook NULL, which reports NA. The default is NULL = unknown, so a node kind added later is over-cautious, never wrong — and a node that has already emitted rows opts out rather than reporting its untouched count. This is deliberately not row_count_hint: that field is an upper bound for collect’s preallocation (a scan reports every stored row even when a pushed-down predicate or zone-map/index pruning will drop some) and is 0, not -1, when unset, so it can neither be trusted for exactness nor distinguish “empty” from “unknown”. Counting a data-dependent plan means a full pass over possibly-larger-than-RAM data, so nrow() reports NA rather than silently starting one; count() |> collect() is the exact-count front door.
  • String ownership: VecArray.owns_data flag distinguishes owned vs borrowed string buffers to avoid double-free in hash join arenas. The orthogonal data_borrowed flag marks buffers that the direct-write tdc decoder landed straight into a caller-supplied SEXP backing store (fixed-width numerics only — strings always allocate).
  • Grouping is metadata-only: group_by() just attaches .groups to the R list; the C-level group_agg node receives key names when summarise() is called.
  • Memory budget is one pool per plan (src/plan_budget.{h,c}, R/memory.R): vec_optimize() ends with vec_plan_assign_budgets(), which walks the plan through each node’s children hook and gives every budgeted node (set_mem_budget set: sort, join, group_agg, fuzzy join, k-mer) a reference-counted VecMemGrant on one VecMemPool of vectra_mem() bytes. Components reserve through a VecMemAcct (vec_mem_try(want): refused means spill; vec_mem_set: forced, for a batch that must be taken, and for releases; vec_mem_allowance) as their allocated footprint grows and shrinks. Each grant owns a floor of total/(4N) it can always reserve; only the rest is shared, first come first served, so the reserved total never exceeds the budget and no node starves another. Composite nodes register once and their internal nodes share the grant (sort_node_share_grant, group_agg_share_grant; grace-hash sub-joins rebind to the parent’s grant). Without a pool (a plan never optimized, e.g. diff_vtr’s internal sorts) an account is a private cap of the node’s own mem_budget. Reservations happen on the master thread between batches, never inside OpenMP regions. Spill runs (sort runs, join and aggregation partitions, fuzzy build runs, the diff_vtr temp file) are written with VTR_SPILL_COMPRESS = VTR_COMPRESS_NONE (written once, read once; measured faster than FAST at equal peak). Regression test: test-memory-bound.R (fresh process, 64 MB budget, peak RSS via internal .peak_rss() from src/proc_mem.c).
  • External sort is bounded on both phases, including the merge (src/sort.c): before appending a batch the sort predicts its buffer’s allocated bytes after the append (vec_builders_bytes_after_batch, builder growth included, one growth rule shared with builder.c) plus 32 B/row of sort scratch (SORT_WORK_BYTES_PER_ROW: permutation plus radix keys and ping-pong buffers) and reserves that on the pool; if refused it spills the current buffer as a sorted run (a batch arriving at an empty buffer is always taken). The in-memory path keeps the buffered columns and one permutation (sort_permutation, shared with run generation) and emits SORT_EMIT_ROWS (131,072)-row batches through gather_batch (fixed-width columns gathered in one OpenMP loop per batch over (column, 8192-row) tasks), so it never holds a second full copy and hands write_vtr() normal row groups (#20: one giant emitted batch was the in-memory slowdown, not the sort). Merge fan-in is capped with multi-pass reduce_runs; compute_merge_fanin sizes it from what the pool would give the merge (measured decoded row width, fan-in * SPILL_RG_SIZE * row_bytes <= allowance/2, clamped to [2, SORT_MAX_FANIN]) and reserves the merge’s bytes. merge_build_one_batch stays the single heap-drain shared by the streaming output and the reduction writer, so the multi-pass path cannot drift from the final merge. Merge sort uses OpenMP tasks above VEC_OMP_THRESHOLD; radix handles single numeric keys.
  • Grouped aggregation is hash-first, spill-bounded (src/group_agg.c, #16/#28): a grouped summarise() of scalar aggregates (sum/mean/min/max/var/sd/n/first/last/any/all) aggregates in up to 64 per-thread hash shards (power of two <= OpenMP threads, split by a mixed key hash hagg_shard_mix), each a VecHashTable + KeyArena + AggAccum[]; a group lives in exactly one shard, so shards run in parallel with no shared state and no merge. Nothing inside that OpenMP region may raise, so capacity is pre-reserved on the master (vec_ht_reserve, key_arena_reserve, agg_accum_reserve). Aggregates whose feed allocates (string first/last; agg_accum_feed_allocates) run one shard serially. The tables are capped at half of what the pool gives the node at start (the result sort keeps the other half); before each batch the cap is re-read from the pool to set the shard freeze point, and after each batch the node reserves what its tables and partition buffers hold. A shard past its share freezes: rows of groups it holds keep aggregating in place, rows of any other group route through part_spill (column map = keys + agg inputs, pid = -1 for rows that stay, salt part_spill_salt(h, depth+1)) into 64 uncompressed partitions, so every group is wholly resident or wholly in one partition and no partial state is merged. Each partition is then aggregated by a nested hash node with a deeper salt; at depth 3 a still-oversized partition takes the sort-based path. Output is ordered by key (NA last): a table that never froze is emitted through an in-RAM merge-sorted permutation; once anything froze the result goes through an external sort sharing the node’s grant. median()/n_distinct() take the sorted path (sorted_agg_next_batch): the input sort shares the grant, keys arrive sorted, accumulators hold one group at a time, and the holistic stores (AggSpill on RecSpill: bit-cast doubles for median, 64-bit value hashes for n_distinct) reserve half the node’s allowance split across the holistic aggregates, spilling to run files and reducing exactly by external merge, so a single huge group costs disk, not RAM. flush_group frees each group’s accumulator before reuse. Measured on 2e7 rows, summarise(n(), mean, sum), 1e3 groups: the old always-sort path 1.9 s / 1.16 GB, now 0.55-0.9 s at under 10 MB over idle.
  • Windows are all spill-safe streaming (src/window.c): no window path materializes the whole table. Grouped windows sort by (keys, row-id) and process one group at a time (window_stream_next, peak = largest group). Ungrouped windows stream the whole partition in a single forward pass (window_ostream_next) with bounded per-spec state, peak = one batch plus the pre-sort’s own spill buffer. window_node_create classifies the ungrouped specs by the stream ordering each needs (win_spec_ord_class): WORD_NATURAL (cumulatives, lag, ntile, unordered row_number — arrival order, no sort), WORD_BY_INPUT (rank family — global sort by the value column), WORD_BY_ORDER (rolling — sort by the time column), WORD_REVERSE (lead — sort by row-id descending, then computed as lag). When every spec shares one ordering it streams. When they do not (mixed ordering classes, or the same class but different value/time columns or sort directions), an ungrouped window with a temp dir decomposes into a chain of single-spec window nodes rather than materializing the whole table: each single spec trivially shares one ordering so each link streams (peak = one batch), and chaining in spec order appends the window columns in exactly the in-memory layout (each link’s rowid-sort-restore-drop returns to arrival order, so composition preserves both column and row order). Every WinKind is individually streamable, so this covers every ungrouped case; the in-memory node now runs only when there is no temp dir to sort/spill through, or for a grouped window without one. Two ordering tricks keep the single-ordering family single-pass: cume_dist sorts descending so count(<= v) = N - rows_streamed is known when a value group opens (no forward peer buffering), and lead becomes lag on the row-id-reversed stream. ntile/percent_rank/cume_dist need the partition size up front, read from the inserted sort via sort_node_total_rows() (the sort knows its exact count once it has consumed its input). The sort/restore/drop-rowid wrapper is shared with the grouped path.
  • Top-N is O(min(k, n)) streaming (src/topn.c): slice_min/slice_max(..., with_ties = FALSE) never materializes its input. A bounded keep-store holds at most k rows (fixed-width values overwritten in place; strings held as per-slot owned copies, freed on eviction) under a size-k max-heap; an incoming row is copied only when it beats the heap root, otherwise it costs one comparison. Peak = the k kept rows, not the whole child. NA in the order column always sorts last, independent of the descending flag, matching dplyr and the with_ties = TRUE R path (order(..., na.last = TRUE)) — an earlier version flipped NA under slice_max and treated it as the maximum.
  • Grouped top-1 is bounded streaming (src/group_topn.c): the n == 1, with_ties = FALSE grouped slice_min/slice_max fast path (the whole winning row per group, geometry column included). It routes the child through a RowIdNode and the bounded external SortNode keyed by (group cols, row-id), so groups arrive contiguous and, within a group, in input order (the row-id is a stable tiebreak). One running champion is kept for the open group; when a group closes its champion is committed to a store that emits in bounded row batches. Peak = one emit batch of winners + one champion + the sort’s own bounded spill — independent of both the input length and the number of groups (the earlier hash-based store held one champion per group resident, O(#groups)). Ties keep the first input row (dplyr semantics), preserved even when the sort spills because the merge stays (key, row-id) ordered. The group-boundary detector KeySnap is shared with group_agg (src/key_snap.{h,c}). Note sort_node_create takes ownership of the SortKey array — do not free it after the call.
  • k-mer counting is spill-safe (src/kmer.c on src/rec_spill.{h,c}): counting distinct (group, k-mer) occurrences no longer holds a hash table that grows with the input (k up to 32, so 4^k is not a real cap). Each observed k-mer window pushes one 16-byte (gid, packed-kmer) record into a RecSpill — a generic fixed-width external sort-merge that spills to run files past mem_budget — then the distinct-count reduction run-length-counts the sorted stream, emitting output batches lazily (cur/cur_count carry an open run across emit batches). Only the group-key arena (one row per distinct group, the natural output cardinality) stays resident. The spill-backed merge closes its run-file handles at stream drain, not at node-free — a streaming node that defers handle release to GC leaks handles across a session (kmer once exhausted the process handle table mid-test-suite, surfacing as a spurious brio “cannot open file” on an unrelated source). RecSpill is the shared engine under the holistic aggregates too: agg_spill’s median / n_distinct are now thin 8-byte consumers of it (src/agg_spill.c), so there is one external-merge implementation, not two.
  • Fuzzy join is streaming-probe, bounded-build (src/fuzzy_join.c): the probe (left) side streams one batch at a time; each probe batch’s matches are computed (OpenMP over the batch’s rows) and emitted in EMIT_BATCH_SIZE chunks. The build (right) side is materialized into builders while its bytes are tracked: if it stays within mem_budget (vectra_mem()) it is held resident and, with a blocking column, indexed by exact block key (BlockIndex, an open-addressing FNV-1a map key -> build rows) — the fast path, one match pass per probe batch, matches ordered (probe row, distance). If the build overflows the budget it is spilled to a .vtr run file in budget-sized rowgroups, and each probe batch is matched against one rowgroup chunk at a time (fuzzy_load_chunk decodes the rowgroup into chunk_cols and builds a per-chunk block index), emitting while that chunk is resident. Peak is then one probe batch + one build rowgroup + that pair’s matches, independent of the build size. The probe stays a single forward pass (never spilled); re-reading the spilled build once per probe batch is the overflow path’s cost, and its output order is per-chunk rather than per-probe-sorted. Resident and spilled paths share one matcher, fuzzy_match_batch_vs(fj, batch, bcols, bnrows, bidx), and one emitter keyed off emit_bcols (which points at b_cols or the current chunk_cols).
  • Interval join is a bounded serial sweep-merge (src/interval_join.c): overlap-joins each probe [start, end] to every build interval it overlaps (optionally within an equality block key). Both sides route through the external sort keyed by (block, start), so neither is held resident; a single forward sweep advances whichever side’s next interval opens first (cursor_order: block then start) and keeps a per-side active set of open intervals. At an open, it evicts opposite-side intervals whose end has passed (< start for closed overlap, <= start for strict), emits the opener against the remaining active opposite set (each active entry carries a one-row column snapshot, IvSnap, so the pair still emits after its source batch is freed), then pushes the opener. Active sets flush at every block boundary and at end; a left join emits an NA-build row for a probe that is evicted/flushed still unmatched. Peak = the two active sets (bounded by overlap depth) + one output batch + the two sorts’ own bounded spill — independent of the input length and the match count (the earlier design materialized both sides, buffered every match, and globally sorted them). Rows with a NA endpoint, start > end, a zero-length interval under strict overlap, or a NA block key are dropped in cursor_advance, matching the prior semantics. The sweep is serial (it gave up the old per-partition OpenMP parallelism) — the deliberate cost of bounding memory.
  • Joins are bounded regardless of key skew (src/join.c): merge-vs-hash is decided from the children’s metadata before the build. The build reserves, before each appended batch, builder capacity after growth plus (hash join only) the slot arrays (16 B/slot, next pow2 >= 2n), chain array and transient hash array, plus full-join’s bitset (join_build_bytes_after); a build side with a metadata row count is sized exactly. A refused reservation grace-hash spills both sides into JOIN_SPILL_PARTS (64) partitions through part_spill (src/part_spill.{h,c}, the one partition-spill writer, shared with group_agg: per-partition buffers written as 65,536-row row groups, buffers bounded to a quarter of the join’s allowance, files created on first write or part_spill_touch, optional column map, pid = -1 = stays resident), salted per depth by part_spill_salt (murmur3 fmix; a bare XOR before % K would only permute buckets and keep colliding keys colliding). The batch that would have overflowed is carried into the spill, not appended. Sub-joins reserve through the parent’s grant, re-partition up to JOIN_MAX_SPILL_DEPTH (3; only a genuine hot key gets that far), then fall to the block-nested-loop, whose blocks are sized by the same reservation (a batch that does not fit is held in bnl_rpending and opens the next block). Resident probe, merge, finalize and BNL share one set of row emitters (join_emit_matched / join_emit_left_only / join_emit_right_only) and one key-coercion pair. Load-bearing, regression-tested invariants: jht.n_build records the true build-row count (not the allocation floored to 1), and the merge path agrees with the hash path (NA keys never match; a cmp>0 unmatched build row is marked in build_matched so finalize does not emit it twice).
  • Two-pass string building: String-producing expressions (gsub, str_extract, paste) compute total output length first, allocate once, then fill — avoids realloc churn.
  • Variable-arity VecExpr: case_when, coalesce, and N-ary paste use a children array on VecExpr rather than fixed left/right operands.
  • Hash index pushdown, opened lazily and stamp-verified: scan.c detects equality predicates (single or AND-combined composite) and probes .vtri sidecar indexes to prune row groups before reading data. Composes with zone-map pruning and binary search on sorted columns. Two properties are load-bearing and regression-tested. (1) The sidecar is opened on the first batch, for the column the predicate actually filters on, not eagerly at tbl() time for the first indexed column in schema order: eager opening read a whole index per tbl() even for queries that could not use it (which is what made an indexed lookup slower than an unindexed one), and the single sn->index slot made every index past the first unreachable. A composite covering the predicate is tried before a single-column index, since it prunes at least as well. (2) An index header stamps the store’s row count, row-group count and fingerprint at build time (VtriStamp, computed by the one function vtri_store_stamp() for both build and check); vtri_open compares them against the store and returns NULL on mismatch, which is the backstop against probing an index whose keys no longer name the row groups they sit in — that would prune groups now holding matching rows and silently drop them from the result. The fingerprint is what catches a same-shape replacement (issue #13: write_vtr(new, f) over an indexed f, or a download/rename over the path); counts alone passed it. write_vtr() also drops the replaced store’s sidecars (.drop_indexes()), and append_vtr() (both directions) takes the pre-append fingerprint (C_store_fingerprint) and passes it to vtri_extend, which carries an index forward only if it described the pre-append store — a column append goes through the same extend (no new row groups, rewrite restamps). A row append does not move existing row groups, so their entries stay true and append_vtr(along = "rows") extends each sidecar instead of rebuilding it (.extend_indexes() in R/index.R -> C_extend_index -> vtri_extend, which scans only the appended row groups and seeds vtri_build_core with the entries already on file). vtri_extend verifies the store opens with the index’s row groups as an unchanged prefix (count not shrunk, those groups still holding exactly the stamped row count) and returns 0 for a full rebuild otherwise. Rebuilding from the whole store on every call would have kept the append quadratic even after the container fix, which is why this exists. has_index() opens the index rather than stat-ing the file, so it reports usability, not presence. Every way of failing to read a sidecar returns NULL, never an error (vtri_open): an index only ever saves a scan work, so an unusable one must cost speed and never rows — raising instead turned a readable store into an unopenable one (issue #11, where a >2 GB index sized with 32-bit ftell failed its own sanity guard and killed tbl()). Allocation failure still raises, being a fact about the machine rather than about the index. (3) An index is read whole only while it is small; past VTRI_RESIDENT_MAX_BYTES (4 MB) it is mapped read-only (src/file_map.c, VecFileMap) and the probe reads entries out of the mapping in place. Reading it whole made every fetch pay for the entire file — 67 ms and 223 MB per open on a 223 MB sidecar, and a 17 GB sidecar would have wanted 17 GB resident per fetch — which is the cost an index exists to avoid; mapped, the same 223 MB index opens below timer resolution and an indexed fetch drops 71.4 ms -> 4.75 ms. Both backings go through the accessors in vtri.h (vtri_entry_hash/vtri_entry_rg/vtri_dir), so the probe and vtri_build_core’s seed merge are written once; the mapping carries no alignment (the header is a whole number of bytes, and an entry is 12), hence the accessors memcpy rather than dereference. An index too large to map reports absent like any other unusable one. A mapped index holds its file open, so vtri_build_core swaps through vtr_atomic_replace (which retries a Windows sharing violation) and closes the seed index before the replacement is moved into place. Verified end to end on a real sidecar over 60M distinct keys (1 ms/open, correct equality and %in% answers).
  • Building an index is bounded too, which is why the entries are sorted rather than chained (src/vtri.c on src/rec_spill.{h,c}): a chained table has to know every entry’s bucket before it can write the first one, so vtri_build_core used to materialize the whole index — 2.23 GB peak resident for the 2.12 GB sidecar over 60M keys, and an index too large for RAM could be read but not made. Entries now go through the shared external sort (RecSpill, 12-byte (hash, rg) records, spilling past vectra_mem()) and are written in one forward pass, so the build’s peak is its sort buffer, the directory, and one decoded row group — none of which grow with the entry count. On the same store: same index at 0.69 GB, built at 0.32 GB peak under a 128 MB budget (0.87 GB at the default, where nothing spills), in the same ~16 s. An extend does not gather either: the sidecar on disk is already a sorted stream, so vtri_extend merges it with the appended row groups’ entries as the new file is written. Sorting by (hash, rg) makes the bytes a function of the data rather than of the scan, so an extended index is byte-identical to a rebuilt one, and a spilled build to an in-RAM one — all three regression-tested. The probe’s cost is held flat by the directory (VTRI_DIR_ENTRIES_PER_SLOT = 4 entries per slot, capped at VTRI_DIR_MAX_BITS = 2^22 slots = 16 MB, the one array the build holds whole): one directory read plus a binary search over ~4 entries, so a fetch stayed at ~40 ms against the chained layout’s ~43 ms rather than paying log2(n_entries) page touches.
  • An index that cannot probe a key must not prune (src/scan.c): the %in% path probed with whichever of set_str/set_i64/set_dbl the predicate carried and silently contributed nothing when none matched the column’s type — so filter(k %in% c(5, 9)) on an integer column (R writes those literals as doubles, so this is the ordinary spelling) OR-ed an empty bitmap, pruned every row group, and returned zero rows where an unindexed store returned all of them. Same for a bool column, and for an NA in the set, whose matching rows the index files under VTRI_NA_HASH. Every element is now probed by the column’s type via int_probe_key, which separates a key no value of that type can equal (fractional or NaN: prune everything, correct) from one that several could (past 2^53 a double stands for several int64 values, so a single probe would prune row groups that match: prune nothing). Anything unprobeable — a type with no probe, a failed allocation — abandons pruning for that scan. test-index.R cross-checks 21 predicate shapes against an unindexed copy of the same store; 7 of them used to disagree.
  • Null-count pruning: scan.c also prunes a row group when a comparison predicate’s column is entirely NA there (null_count >= rg_n_rows). The comparison is NA for every row, which the filter drops, so the group can be skipped. null_count is carried through vtr1_tdc_decode_stat independent of has_stats (an all-NA numeric column has no min/max but a valid null count), so this fires even where zone maps cannot.
  • No Robin Hood hashing: Benchmarked Robin Hood with displacement cascades and early termination on both VecHashTable (group_agg, 70% load) and JoinHT (joins, 50% load). Result: 12-29% regressions. FNV-1a already distributes well enough that average probe length is ~1.3-1.7 at these load factors — too short for Robin Hood’s variance reduction to outweigh the per-probe overhead of maintaining and checking displacement distances. Don’t re-attempt without evidence of long probe chains in production workloads.
  • Default batch_size = 131072: 131072 rows per row group (~1 MB per double column). Keeps the decode working set in L2/L3 cache. Benchmarked ~21% faster reads vs one-giant-row-group at no file-size cost. Sweet spot is 100K–500K rows.
  • Compression internals live in tdc: The LZ matcher, wildcopy fast/safe decode split, byte-shuffle SIMD kernels, spatial predictor kernels, and the “don’t batch parse-then-copy” benchmark result all live in tdc/CLAUDE.md now. Don’t re-tune any of that here — treat tdc as the compression authority and consult its CLAUDE.md before attempting optimization.
  • String dict-defer: A TDC_MODEL_DICT_1D string column decodes to (unique values + per-row indices), so collect() interns each unique CHARSXP once and fills by index instead of once per row. Three pieces:
    • tdc primitive: tdc_decode_block_dict (tdc/src/api/decode_dict.c) decodes a DICT_1D block into (dictionary bytes + u32 indices) WITHOUT flattening, reusing the shared decode pipeline via a run_model = 0 hook. Exercised by C_tdc_dict_roundtrip (test-dict-defer.R).
    • Carrier: VecArray.str_dict (VecStrDict in src/types.h) is an optional dictionary side-channel for a VEC_STRING array — unique values + indices, with buf.str left as the placeholder and NA rows in validity as usual. It is produced ONLY by the collect direct-read decode (vtr_decode_column_tdc_dict in src/vtr_codec_tdc.c, reached when the read path is called with defer_str_dict != 0 — vtr1_read_rowgroup_tdc_defer / vtr1_read_parallel_tdc_defer_into) and consumed ONLY by the collect string fill (fill_string_col_from_dict in src/collect.c); it never reaches a filter/join/project/window node, so no other consumer has to understand it. Freed by vec_array_free via vec_str_dict_free. The non-DICT_1D string block (currently unreachable — every string column is DICT_1D since the compress="none" fix) falls back to the flat decode.
    • Fill: fill_string_col_from_dict interns each dict entry lazily on first use (its CHARSXP is reachable through the PROTECTed output column thereafter) through the shared intern_str_cached helper, so both within-batch (rows -> unique) and cross-batch (StrCacheSlot cache) dedup apply. Measured: on 5M rows of wide (~40-char) heavily-duplicated strings, collect drops from ~0.34s (flat per-row intern) to ~0.03s — the CHARSXP fill was the dominant cost. array_to_sexp / batch_to_dataframe route strings through the same fill, so they are dict-safe for free.

Vendored libraries and release workflow

tdc (typed dimensional compression)

Source of truth: gcol33/tdc (public GitHub repo), lives locally at ../tdc/ as a sibling directory. Vectra vendors a snapshot of tdc’s include/ and src/ into src/tdc/ at build time.

  • src/tdc/ is tracked in git (the vendored snapshot is committed) so GitHub-HEAD installs (pak/remotes) and CRAN tarballs are self-contained without the sibling repo. configure/configure.win still re-vendor fresh from ../tdc/ when the sibling is present (development); the committed copy is the fallback. Build artifacts (*.o/*.so/*.dll) stay ignored.
  • configure / configure.win auto-vendor from ../tdc/ on every R CMD INSTALL / devtools::load_all(). Falls back to a pre-vendored copy if the sibling repo is absent (CRAN tarball install).
  • tools/vendor_tdc.sh is the vendoring script (called by configure, can also run manually). Stamps src/tdc/VENDORED_FROM with the source commit hash.
  • CI workflows all check out gcol33/tdc as a sibling via actions/checkout@v4 before building.

miniz

Single-file deflate library at src/miniz/. Powers TIFF deflate strips and gzip CSV input. Tracked in git (rarely changes).

Releasing

Tag-driven via .github/workflows/release.yml:

git tag v0.4.3
git push origin v0.4.3

The workflow: checks out vectra + tdc → vendors tdc → R CMD build → R CMD check → creates GitHub Release with the self-contained .tar.gz. That tarball is what goes to CRAN (includes src/tdc/ so no external dependency needed at install time).

Bench scripts (bench_*.R)

The repo root contains a pile of one-off bench_*.R scripts left over from the LZ/decode-tuning era. They are not part of the package build, just sandbox scripts for ad-hoc throughput measurements. Status as of 2026-04-07:

  • Still useful (rewired to current compress = c("fast", "none") API):
    • bench_refresh.R — read/write matrix vs fst/parquet on 5M×8 doubles
    • bench_zstd.R — vectra fast vs fst zstd levels vs saveRDS
    • bench_vs_zstd.R — same but also runs zstd CLI on the raw byte stream
    • bench_compress_final.R — 2000² f64 raster vs terra DEFLATE (kept fresh, feeds the vectra row in tdc/bench/RESULTS.md)
  • Obsolete compress = "ratio" removed — "ratio" was the shuffle+deflate path; deflate is gone now that the codec is tdc. The three scripts above had their "ratio" cases dropped (not patched to "fast", because "fast" was already a separate row in each script).
  • Other bench_*.R scripts in the root are even older (joins, sort, IO, TIFF, parallel, profiling helpers). They predate the codec rewire and don’t reference codec internals — they should still run, but no one has touched them in a while. Treat them as scratch, not as a regression suite.

If you add a new throughput measurement, prefer extending bench_refresh.R over creating yet another bench_*.R file.
